question: Should generated systemd-unit provenance become a first-class shared SQLite state record, or is an exception for a file-backed sidecar intended?
rationale: The repository policy selects SQLite for OpenClaw runtime state, while this PR creates a new JSON store; deciding whether an exception is acceptable is an ownership decision rather than a mechanical review choice.

options.title: Use shared SQLite provenance
options.body: Rework the PR to add a narrowly scoped shared-state record and retain the existing suggested-unit behavior for modified or legacy units.

options.title: Approve a documented sidecar exception
options.body: Keep the JSON design only if maintainers explicitly define its lifecycle, migration, backup, and removal contract outside the normal SQLite rule.

recommendation.title: Use shared SQLite provenance
recommendation.body: Rework the PR to add a narrowly scoped shared-state record and retain the existing suggested-unit behavior for modified or legacy units.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored both the state-storage boundary and the canonical provenance issue.
